data.body: DSH vs Aworkit cache gap is not an accounting artifact. Both read the same provider fields: Aworkit rows satisfy hit+miss==input on all 210 turns; DSH steps satisfy totalTokens==input+cacheRead+output on all 79. Side by side (uncached per step): DSH median 212, max 14,540 (its cold start), one step >2,000, total 36,540 of which 14,540 is the cold start, so steady state ~282/step. Aworkit new: median 629, 18 turns >2,000 summing 104,453 (64% of uncached), max 25,318. Aworkit old: median 695, 17 turns >2,000 summing 168,967 (75%), max 39,005. So DSH never breaks its prefix; Aworkit re-bills its whole context ~18 times per run. Aworkit also appends ~3x more novel tokens per turn. Note the reasoning replay flatters Aworkit: ~26% of its cached tokens are provider-added reasoning, so its 98.4% hit rate overstates its real prefix reuse. Fix target is prefix stability, not more caching.
